title: Translator's Note
html:
The Sri Krishna-Chaitanya-charitamrita is the Sanskrit mahakavya (great poem) of Kavi Karnapura (Paramananda Sena), the youngest son of Shivananda Sena, who as a child received Mahaprabhu's mercy. The poem in twenty sargas was completed in 1464 Shaka (1542 CE), in the month of Ashadha (20.49); the author's main source, he says, was the notes of Murari Gupta (20.42–43). It opens with the lament of the devotees after the Lord's disappearance and then tells His whole life, from His appearance in Navadvipa to the last years in Puri, with special fullness for the Ratha-yatra and the festivals of Nilachala.

Source. The Sanskrit text follows the edition of Haridasa Shastri (Vrindavana), checked by hand against the scan; 1,912 verses by our count. Only Karnapura's text is translated; the translations and commentaries of the editions are not included. Interpretation follows Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati.
